speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing; could you tell me if these symptoms worsen specifically when you cry, feed, or lie on your back?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD). The presence of stridor worsening with neck flexion and crying, combined with post-prandial vomiting in an infant, strongly supports this diagnosis.
